findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) present at the facility when the inspector arrived. During the inspection a CFPM arrived at the facility. The inspector suggests more employees getting CFPM certificates. Ensure that there is always a CFPM present during all hours of food preparation and handling.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee used their bare hands to operate the faucets after hand washing. The employee was educated about the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucets to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPART VIOLATION: Observed the hand washing sink was blocked with a sanitizer bucket when the inspector arrived at the facility. The bucket was removed and the employee was educated. Ensure that the hand washing sink is maintained accessible at all times for employee use.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the bottom right gasket of the freezer is in a state of disrepair partially unattached. The gasket must be either repaired or replaced to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the gasket is fixed by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the employee working does not have a food handler certificate. Ensure that all employees who do not have CFPM certificates complete the food handler training by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Observed there was not a CFPM at the facility when the inspector arrived. The PIC is a CFPM and arrived at the facility during the inspection. The inspector suggests getting employees who usually work during breakfast hours certified. Ensure there is always a CFPM at the facility when food is being prepared and served.

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed the hand sink was blocked with a sanitizer bucket when the inspector arrived. The sanitizer bucket was removed from the hand sink during the inspection. Ensure the hand washing sink is always accessible to employees. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Observed the bottom gasket on the right door of the freezer is in disrepair. The gasket must be repaired to create a strong seal on the freezer and maintain equipment in good repair. Ensure the gasket is repaired or replaced by the next routine inspection. 

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed the employee working did not have their food handler training. All food handlers (except if they have their CFPM certificate) must obtain training in basic food handling principles. Ensure that all employees receive the food handler training by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.comment:
Facility is a medium-risk facility. Inspector observed a clear plastic container properly date marked indicating that the container held “gravy mix” which had been prepared on 11/17/2022 and was to be discarded on 11/20/2022. Using an IR temperature gun, inspector obtained a reading of 97 degrees F indicating that the gravy mix had been cooked and was in the process of cooling. Operator stated that the food was prepared around 8:00 AM today and was intended to be reheated on Saturday, 11/20/2022, for service. Facility was immediately advised that operation under a medium-risk permit is limited to same day service and that cooling and reheating is not allowed within the scope of their current permit. The gravy mix was immediately discarded voluntarily by the facility. Inspector had a long discussion with both operators regarding permit limitations and alternate procedures. Corrected on site. Facility will cook gravy daily as needed for service and will discard upon completion of food service. Establishment will not be upgrading to a high-risk permit. Ensure that food preparation occurs within the scope of the facility’s permit with Sangamon County. No follow-up is required at this time. 

3-201.11: (A)-(B) FOOD shall be obtained from APPROVED source and not from private home. P (C) PACKAGED Food shall be properly labeled. (E) WHOLE-MUSCLE BEEF shall be from approved source and acceptable from AUTHROITY. Pf (D) FISH must be frozen if consumed undercooked. (F) Meat and Poultry shall be properly labeled.
